newsitem.title: USA: Lead boat in Cuban flotilla seized by US officials.
newsitem.headline: Lead boat in Cuban flotilla seized by US officials.

text.p: The U.S. Coast Guard seized a boat that was to lead an exile protest flotilla sailing toward Cuba on Sunday after its pilots would not promise to keep it out of Cuban territorial waters.
"We seized the vessel 'Democracia'," Coast Guard spokeswoman Petty Officer Veronica Bandrowsky said.
She said no one was arrested when the boat was escorted to a Coast Guard station after leaving Key West, Florida. About 13 other boats were allowed to proceed toward Cuba's coast early on Sunday.
"The vessel Democracia was the only vessel that stated that it had intention to enter Cuban territorial seas," Bandrowsky said.

Ramon Saul Sanchez, head of the Cuban exile group Democracy Movement, was on board the seized boat. He said on Saturday that U.S. officials had promised to arrest him as soon as he left the dock in the latest in a series of waterborne protests against the island's communist regime by Cubans living in Florida.

Sunday's protesters planned a ceremony on the high seas outside the 12-mile (19-km) limit of Cuba's territorial waters to mark the anniversary of the drowning of 41 people as they attempted to leave the island on July 13, 1994.
Sanchez had pledged to pilot a small boat to the site eight miles (13 km) north of Havana where the 41 people died.
Members of the exile group Brothers to the Rescue also promised to join the flotilla on Sunday, participating in a fly over as part of the protest memorial.

The United States, which warned flotilla participants to respect Cuba's territory, has urged Cuba's government to act prudently toward the flotilla. The Cuban government regards the flotillas as provocations.

Before allowing them to depart, the Coast Guard boarded each vessel and made sure they complied with safety regulations. Coast Guard vessels were in the Florida Straits to keep track of the flotilla boats as they proceeded, Bandrowsky said.

In February 1996 Cuban MiG fighters shot down two small planes piloted by members of Brothers to the Rescue near the island, killing the four Cuban-American crew members and sparking a diplomatic crisis.
